def:
1. the system of communication in speech and writing that is used by people of a particular country or area
2. the use by humans of a system of sounds and words to communicate
3. a particular style of speaking or writing
★ Collocations: first language; native language; foreign language
★ Word family: linguistic (adj); linguist (n)

1. a person, an object, an event, etc. that represents a more general quality or situation
2. a sign, number, letter, etc. that has a fixed meaning, especially in science, mathematics and music
★ Collocations: dramatic symbol; important symbol; perfect symbol
★ Word family: (see OALD for derivatives)

1. an event, an action, a fact, etc. that shows that something exists, is happening or may happen in the future
2. a piece of paper, wood or metal that has writing or a picture on it that gives you information, instructions, a warning, etc.
3. a movement or sound that you make to tell somebody something
★ Collocations: classic sign; clear sign; definite sign
★ Word family: (see OALD for derivatives)

1. a movement that you make with your hands, your head or your face to show a particular meaning
2. something that you do or say to show a particular feeling or intention
★ Collocations: dramatic gesture; expansive gesture; expressive gesture
★ Word family: (see OALD for derivatives)

1. writing that is done with a pen or pencil, not printed or typed
2. a person’s particular style of writing in this way
3. used when you are describing a situation in which there are signs that something is going to have problems or that it is going to be a failure
★ Collocations: clear handwriting; good handwriting; legible handwriting
★ Word family: (see OALD for derivatives)

1. a picture representing a word or phrase
2. a diagram that uses pictures to represent amounts or numbers of a particular thing
★ Collocations: Emojis—pictographs used in instant messagi
★ Word family: (see OALD for derivatives)

1. a piece of wood, rubber, metal, etc. with one thick end and one thin, pointed end that you use to keep a door open, to keep two things apart, or to split wood or rock
2. something that is like a wedge
3. a shoe with a wedge
★ Collocations: He hammered the wedge into the crack in the st; a wedge of cake/cheese; shoes with wedge heels
★ Word family: (see OALD for derivatives)

1. a join made by tying together two pieces or ends of string, rope, etc.
2. a way of twisting
3. a tight mass in something such as hair or wool, where it has become twisted
★ Collocations: loose knot; tight knot; tangled knot
★ Word family: (see OALD for derivatives)

1. the scientific study of language or of particular languages

1. connected with the meaning of words and sentences

1. the way that words and phrases are put together to form sentences in a language; the rules of grammar for this

1. to make the sound of a word or letter in a particular way

1. relating to words

1. a word or phrase
